Hi Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick written recap so we have a shared record and clear next steps. I tried to capture the key pain points and the bar for a Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) pilot. Please correct anything I got wrong.

What you told us (pain / goal):
- Current failure mode: bursty inference load during end-of-quarter reporting causes both unpredictable latency spikes and token cost blowouts.
- Security/controls: data residency requirement in US-East, customer-managed KMS for key material, and audit logs retained 12 months.
- Isolation: you need logical isolation (dedicated pool) rather than shared tenancy due to compliance and SLA promises to your customers.

Current stack and telemetry you shared:
- Serving: in-house inference service (Python + Triton) calling standard transformers for ranking and summarization.
- Peak traffic: ~280 TPS for short bursts (~3–5 min), sustained baseline 30–50 TPS.
- Typical sequence length: 256 tokens (ranking) and 1,024 tokens (summarization).
- p95 latency target: <= 120ms for ranking endpoints (95% of requests).

Success criteria for an eval/pilot:
- Achieve p95 <= 120ms at 250 TPS for ranking workload in a dedicated pool.
- Demonstrate predictable unit cost within 15% of our estimate.
- KMS integration and audit logs available for the pilot environment.
- Autoscale/burst policy that can handle 5x baseline when configured without noisy neighbor interference.

Constraints and assumptions from our side:
- Reserved pool will be provisioned in US-East and configured for model variants you bring (we'll validate model graph compatibility and quantization).
- Autoscaling has a warmup window (typically 45–90s for a cold GPU VM); we can provide burst capacity with pre-warm options for short spikes.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) I’ll share a draft pilot SOW and a preliminary capacity estimate (attached). Please confirm: are the TPS numbers above correct for your ranking endpoint?
2) We schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra + model owners (30–45 min) — Dev from our infra team will walk through kernel selection, KV cache behavior, and cold-start mitigation.
3) We’ll scope an isolation plan (networking, KMS, audit log retention) and map it to your compliance checklist.

Proposed meeting windows next week: Mon 12/7 10:00–11:00 ET or Tue 12/8 14:00–15:00 ET.

Attached: capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with rough GPU/day and cost estimates), pilot_sow_draft.pdf (high-level pilot scope).

If that all looks good I’ll follow up with a calendar invite and the SOW.

Best,

— Logan Wright

Hi Priya — quick tech notes ahead of the deep-dive. Copying the items that affect the pilot SOW.

1) HSM/KMS: Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys via an HSM-backed KMS integration. For a pilot we can provision a dedicated key policy bound to the pilot VPC; we’ll need an IAM principal and a key policy to validate access.

2) Autoscale and burst handling: our Dedicated pools support two mechanisms:
   - Reactive autoscale: spins additional nodes when queue depth increases (45–90s warmup depending on model size).
   - Pre-warmed burst slots: reserved ephemeral GPUs that are kept in a pre-warmed state for <5 min spikes (configurable, counted against pilot quota).

3) Cold-start mitigation: suggest using KV cache priming (we can pre-populate with common prefix contexts) and a short-lived warmup traffic generator during pilot windows to reduce p95 during scheduled spikes.

4) Metrics we’ll collect in the pilot: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, per-model throughput, GPU utilization, token cost per 1k requests, and audit-log events for each request (timestamp, request id, model version).

Request from your team before the deep-dive: can you share a small sample trace (anonymized) showing a 60–120s spike and the accompanying model/sequence length distribution? That will help us size pre-warmed capacity more accurately.

I’ll prepare a short runbook and an ops checklist to attach to the SOW.

— Dev
